source.objectiveEnglishInternal: state a seating preference, explain your reason, and accept or propose a compromise
source.roleplayEnglishInternal: A server asks your group to move to a smaller table for a reservation; explain why you'd like to stay and reach a compromise.
source.readerTitleSpanish: Una mesa junto a la ventana

readerVerbExamples.target: Preferimos esta mesa porque tenemos un cochecito.
readerVerbExamples.native: We prefer this table because we have a stroller.

readerVerbExamples.target: Si es posible, nos quedamos aquí hasta las 10:15.
readerVerbExamples.native: If possible, we will stay here until 10:15.

readerVerbExamples.target: Después nos movemos a la terraza.
readerVerbExamples.native: Afterward we move to the patio.

archivedDraft.scene: Staff needs a reserved table; Sam’s family checks another space that can fit the stroller.

sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: A male server is mesero; in Spain you also hear camarero/camarera.
Common in Mexico and the US; in Spain people usually say reserva.
Rincón is an inside corner of a room; esquina is a street corner.
You will also hear carriola in Mexico.
The outdoor seating area of a café or restaurant.

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Preferimos esta mesa porque tenemos un cochecito.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: We prefer this table because we have a stroller.
sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: Giving a reason with porque makes your request sound polite, not demanding.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: ベビーカーがあるので、このテーブルがいいです。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: We prefer this table because we have a stroller.

sourceCards.sourceEnglish: What time does the reservation arrive?
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 予約のお客さんは何時に来ますか。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: What time does the reservation arrive?

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: ¿Qué le parece si terminamos antes de las 10:15?
sourceCards.sourceNoteInternal: ¿Qué le parece si...? is a polite way to suggest a compromise to one person (usted).
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 10時15分より前に食べ終えるのはいかがでしょうか。

sourceCards.sourceSpanish: Si es posible, nos gustaría quedarnos aquí.
sourceCards.sourceEnglish: If possible, we would like to stay here.
sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: 可能でしたら、この席に座っていたいのですが。
sourceCards.literalJapaneseGlossEn: If possible, we would like to stay here.

sourceCards.targetJapaneseDraft: わかりました。事情は理解しました。

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Es sábado por la mañana y mi familia desayuna en una mesa grande junto a la ventana.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: It is Saturday morning and my family is having breakfast at a big table by the window.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 土曜日の朝、私の家族は窓際の大きなテーブルで朝食を食べています。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: It is Saturday morning and my family is having breakfast at a big table by the window.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: La mesera se acerca y dice: Disculpen, tenemos una reservación y necesitamos esta mesa.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The server comes over and says: Excuse me, we have a reservation and we need this table.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 女性の店員がやって来て、こう言います。「すみません、予約が入っていて、このテーブルが必要なんです。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The server comes over and says: Excuse me, we have a reservation and we need this table.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Ella nos ofrece una mesa más pequeña en el rincón, cerca de la barra.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: She offers us a smaller table in the corner, near the counter.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 店員はカウンター近くの隅にある、もっと小さなテーブルを勧めてくれます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: She offers us a smaller table in the corner, near the counter.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Le explico con calma: Preferimos esta mesa porque tenemos un cochecito y no cabe en el rincón.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: I calmly explain to her: We prefer this table because we have a stroller and it does not fit in the corner.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 私は落ち着いて説明します。「ベビーカーがあるので、このテーブルがいいです。隅の席にはベビーカーが入りません。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: I calmly explain to her: We prefer this table because we have a stroller and it does not fit in the corner.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Luego le pregunto: ¿A qué hora llega la reservación?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: Then I ask her: What time does the reservation arrive?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: それから店員に尋ねます。「予約のお客さんは何時に来ますか。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: Then I ask her: What time does the reservation arrive?

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: La mesera responde que el grupo llega a las 10:30.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: The server answers that the group arrives at 10:30.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 店員は、そのグループが10時30分に来ると答えます。
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: The server answers that the group arrives at 10:30.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Entonces propongo: ¿Qué le parece si terminamos el desayuno aquí antes de las 10:15 y después nos movemos a la terraza para el café?
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: So I propose: What if we finish breakfast here before 10:15 and then move to the patio for coffee?
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: そこで私は提案します。「10時15分より前にここで朝食を食べ終えて、そのあとコーヒーを飲むためにテラス席に移るのはどうでしょうか。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: So I propose: What if we finish breakfast here before 10:15 and then move to the patio for coffee?

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Ella sonríe y dice: Perfecto, en la terraza hay sombra y les traigo una silla extra.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: She smiles and says: Perfect, there is shade on the patio and I will bring you an extra chair.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 店員は笑顔で言います。「いいですね。テラス席には日陰がありますし、椅子をもう一脚お持ちします。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: She smiles and says: Perfect, there is shade on the patio and I will bring you an extra chair.

sourceSettingReader.speaker: Narrator
sourceSettingReader.sourceSpanish: Le digo: Muchas gracias por su ayuda, así todos estamos contentos.
sourceSettingReader.sourceEnglish: I tell her: Thank you very much for your help, this way we are all happy.
sourceSettingReader.targetJapaneseDraft: 私は店員に言います。「ご協力ありがとうございます。こうすればみんなが満足できます。」
sourceSettingReader.literalJapaneseGlossEn: I tell her: Thank you very much for your help, this way we are all happy.

japaneseSpecificFocusCandidate: State a seating preference, explain that the stroller does not fit the proposed corner table, ask when the reserved group arrives, and propose a timed move to the patio.
speakingGoalInternal: A server asks your group to move to a smaller table for a reservation; explain why you'd like to stay and reach a compromise.
speakingGoalJapaneseDraft: 店員から、予約のために小さなテーブルへ移ってほしいと言われました。ベビーカーが入らない理由を説明し、予約のお客さんが来る時間を聞いて、妥協案を提案してください。
sourceConflictInternal: The current source is a nine-turn Saturday family breakfast scene: a female server needs the big window table for a 10:30 reservation, offers a smaller corner table near the counter, hears that a stroller will not fit, and accepts a plan to finish before 10:15 then move to the shaded patio for coffee with an extra chair. The archived Sam scene instead adds aisle clearance and an inspection before agreeing; those are not current source facts. Japanese locale, gender marking, patio meaning and dictionary senses need qualified review.

reviewQuestionsInternal.note: English source explicitly says the server is female. Japanese 女性の店員 makes that explicit where needed; 店員 alone later avoids awkward repetition. Qualified Japanese reviewer should decide whether the marked gender is natural in this teaching context.

Source rincón is an inside corner near the counter, not a street corner. 部屋の隅 in the card and 隅 in Reader preserve this. The archived draft instead adds an aisle inspection not present in current source.
English patio means outdoor café seating here. テラス席 is a contextual candidate, not a general equivalence for every patio. Source Spanish terraza and locale need dictionary review.

The card says “We prefer”; Japanese ベビーカーがあるので、このテーブルがいいです expresses the group preference without an overt plural subject. Reader includes that the stroller does not fit the corner; card does not add that separate fact.

The English question says the reservation arrives, then Reader clarifies a group arriving at 10:30. Japanese question names 予約のお客さん, avoiding the unnatural claim that a booking itself walks in. Reviewer to assess equivalence.
Card finishes before 10:15; Reader finishes breakfast here before 10:15 and moves to the patio for coffee. Japanese keeps the time and sequence. Source says strictly before 10:15, not at or by 10:15.
Shade, an extra chair, and mutual satisfaction are retained. Japanese last line uses みんなが満足できます for “we are all happy”; reviewer to assess the satisfaction/happiness nuance.
Mesera/mesero, reservación/reserva, rincón/esquina, carriola and ¿Qué le parece si...? notes are Spanish-specific and remain internal. None are Japanese teaching.

Archived draft has 12 cards and nine dialogue turns with different people and aisle-safety facts. Candidate has 15 source-order cards and nine source-aligned Reader turns. Old rows have no explicit IDs; string overlap is text-only and neither saved-item nor audio migration is authorized.
